module_summary: vmc_groups.cpp is an embedded title-id to memory-card-group dictionary (97 groups, 1046 entries) with one linear lookup, getGroupIdForTitleId, used by guigame.cpp to name per-series VMC images. vmcsaves.cpp/.h is a self-contained PS2 memory-card filesystem reader/writer that edits VMC images in place (list, export/import save folders, PSU pack/unpack, delete) for the VMC dialog in guigame.cpp and the File Manager in guifilemgr.cpp. xparam.cpp/.h applies DECKARD (slim PS2 / PS3 emu) XPARAM compatibility settings by loading rom0:XPARAM with per-title arguments; ResetDeckardXParams is called from opl.cpp main and ApplyDeckardXParam from system.cpp before a game boots. All three .cpp files are compiled into the main riptopl ELF (ps2.yaml:641).

reusable_helpers.name: vsReadAll / vsWriteAll
reusable_helpers.what: static: read or write a whole buffer through read()/write() in 64 KB pieces, 0 on a short transfer

reusable_helpers.name: vmcSavesTitle
reusable_helpers.what: icon.sys head to its title as plain ASCII (both lines joined), public

reusable_helpers.name: vsSjisToAscii
reusable_helpers.what: static: Shift-JIS full-width letters/digits/punctuation to ASCII, drops kana/kanji

reusable_helpers.name: vsStamp
reusable_helpers.what: static: time_t to an 8-byte sceMcStDateTime stamp in JST

reusable_helpers.name: vsOpen
reusable_helpers.what: static: parse a VMC superblock, detect ECC (.ps2) layout, load the indirect FAT and FAT

reusable_helpers.name: vsLoadPsu / vsWritePsu
reusable_helpers.what: static: parse and write PSU single-file saves (write goes to .tmp then rename)

reusable_helpers.name: getGroupIdForTitleId
reusable_helpers.what: title id to shared memory-card group id, or the title id itself

findings.title: vmc_groups.cpp: eight malformed title ids can never match a startup id
findings.problem: getGroupIdForTitleId does an exact strcmp (vmc_groups.cpp:1465) against the game's startup id (guigame.cpp:493,529), which has the dotted 11-char form SLUS_207.54. Entries SLUS_20754, SLUS_20824, SCES_50422, SLES_50422, SCES_51154, SLES_51154, SLES-5350 and SSCES_540.95 lack the dot, use a dash or have an extra letter, so these games never get their series VMC and silently fall back to a per-game card.
findings.fix: Correct the eight strings to the dotted form (SLUS_207.54, SLUS_208.24, SCES_504.22, SLES_504.22, SCES_511.54, SLES_511.54, SCES_540.95; SLES-5350 is most likely SLES_535.06, next to SCES_535.06 at line 496). None of the corrected ids is already in the table.
findings.benefit: Minor bug fixed: 8 titles get their shared group card. 0 lines, 0 bytes.
findings.evidence: Parsed all 97 arrays with a script: 8 ids fail the 11-char XXXX_NNN.NN shape, at lines 443,444,464,465,472,473,498,614. tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:16-17,29 counts these as a KNOWN DATA ISSUE but does not assert. Grep for the dotted forms in vmc_groups.cpp: no matches. Caller format (dotted startup id from CONFIG_ITEM_STARTUP or gsOf(support)->startup) is INFERRED from guigame.cpp:521-529 and the dotted form of the other 1038 entries; the intended id for SLES-5350 is INFERRED.

findings.title: vmc_groups.cpp: two whole groups (XEBP_100.72, XEBP_000.12) and five duplicate entries are unreachable
findings.problem: The lookup returns the first group in table order (vmc_groups.cpp:1459-1469). XEBP_100.72 (1149-1152) repeats XEBP_100.71's three ids exactly (1144-1146) and every XEBP_000.12 id (1272-1275) is already in XEBP_100.53 (936-939), so both groups can never be returned. Lines 668, 676, 1029, 1057, 1226 repeat an id already listed earlier in the same group.
findings.fix: Delete the titles_XEBP_100_72 and titles_XEBP_000_12 arrays with their count lines and table rows, and the five in-group duplicate lines. Behaviour is unchanged. XEBP_100.72 looks like a copy-paste of 100.71 (the history comment at 1153 says the same), so whoever owns the data may want to look up its real titles instead.
findings.benefit: ~20 source lines; ~12 dead entries x (12-byte string + 4-byte pointer) + 2 x 12-byte rows = ~215 bytes of ELF data (INFERRED arithmetic).
findings.evidence: Script over the file in table order: 1046 entries, 1034 distinct; duplicates at 668(of 665), 676(675), 1029(1028), 1057(1053), 1150-1152(1144-1146, group 100_71), 1226(1222), 1272-1275(936-939, group 100_53). Every entry of 100_72 and 000_12 is shadowed. Read lines 1143-1153, 1266-1276, 1424, 1439, 1452-1474. tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:15-17 calls these a known data issue without asserting.

findings.title: vmc_groups.cpp: 97 count_ constants and the titleCount field can go if the arrays are NULL-terminated
findings.problem: Each of the 97 groups has a hand-written count_X = sizeof(titles_X)/sizeof(titles_X[0]) line (1344 is one of them) feeding a titleCount field. The pattern has already broken: the comments at 1153, 1158, 1172, 1180 record four copy-pasted numerators that overstated the count and walked past the array.
findings.fix: End each titles_ array with NULL on its closing line, drop the titleCount field and all 97 count_ lines (with the four 'was sizeof' history comments), and loop while titleIds[j] != NULL. Update tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:25-26, which reads titleCount.
findings.benefit: ~98 source lines removed (97 count lines + 1 field). ELF data about equal: -97 x 4-byte titleCount, +97 x 4-byte NULL (INFERRED). Removes the class of out-of-bounds bug the comments describe.
findings.evidence: Script: 97 titles_ arrays, 97 table rows (1353-1449), each with a count_ constant. Read 1-40, 1138-1185, 1340-1474. Only users of the struct: getGroupIdForTitleId (1452-1474) and tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:12-34 (includes the .cpp). include/vmc_groups.h exposes only the function.

findings.title: xparam.h: 18 PARAM_* constants unused and included by 8 files that use nothing from it
findings.problem: PARAM_MDEC_DELAY_CYCLE..PARAM_CACHE_FLASH_CHANNELS (xparam.h:12-29) are referenced only in comments in xparam.cpp:146-163 and in docs/xparam/*.c, which no build compiles. GM_IOP_TYPE and GM_IF are used only in xparam.cpp. Of the 11 files that include xparam.h, only opl.cpp (ResetDeckardXParams, :2069) and system.cpp (ApplyDeckardXParam, :1511) use it.
findings.fix: Delete the 18 PARAM_* lines, move GM_IOP_TYPE and GM_IF into xparam.cpp, leaving the header with the two prototypes (add an include guard while there), and delete the 8 unneeded #include lines.
findings.benefit: ~26 source lines; no ELF change (constexpr ints emit nothing) (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: git grep -nE 'PARAM_[A-Z0-9_]+|ResetDeckardXParams|ApplyDeckardXParam|xparam.h|GM_IOP_TYPE|GM_IF' outside docs/ and xparam.cpp: PARAM_* only in xparam.h (and unrelated MBEDTLS_/SPISD_ names); includes in autolaunch, lwnbdctl, opl, settingsio, sysdisc, sysneutrino, system, sysvmc, appscan, menuitems; calls only opl.cpp:2069 and system.cpp:1511. docs/xparam is referenced only by docs/DOCUMENTATION-GAPS.md:112, not by ps2.yaml.

findings.title: xparam.cpp: the same DCACHE_OFF / CPU_DELAY loads, DECKARD check and rom0 probes are written out several times
findings.problem: The memcpy(params_DCACHE_OFF)+SifLoadModule pair appears three times (79-80, 109-110, 225-226) and the CPU_DELAY pair twice (97-98, 112-113); ApplyExtraXParamTitle returns from each branch instead of setting flags. The DECKARD bit test and its 6-line comment are repeated (123-130, 196-203), and open/close probes of rom0:XPARAM2 and rom0:XPARAM appear four times. params_DCACHE_OFF and params_CPU_DELAY are writable globals used only here.
findings.fix: In ApplyExtraXParamTitle compute two flags (dcacheOff, cpuDelay) from the three title lists and issue each load once at the end; let the special-disc path at 222-227 reuse that tail. Keep one copy of the DECKARD comment. Make the two params_ arrays static const.
findings.benefit: ~12 source lines; a few dozen bytes of code (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read xparam.cpp 1-246 in full. git grep params_DCACHE_OFF / params_CPU_DELAY outside xparam.cpp: no matches (so static is safe).

findings.title: vmcsaves.cpp re-implements its own helpers: vsReadIn's cluster loop, vsLoadFolder's name check, read/write loops
findings.problem: vsReadIn's inner loop (427-434) is vsReadChain (364-372) for a shorter size. vsLoadFolder's name test (643) is a weaker copy of vsNameOk (767-770, which also rejects '.' and '..'). vsReadAll and vsWriteAll (145-169) differ only in read versus write.
findings.fix: Replace vsReadIn's loop with 'return vsReadChain(v, e.cluster, buf, n) ? n : -1'; move vsNameOk above vsLoadFolder and call it at 643; fold vsReadAll/vsWriteAll into one function with a writing flag, as vsIo already does at 173.
findings.benefit: ~12 source lines; under 200 bytes of code (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 1-1257 in full. vsReadChain adds only a size-larger-than-card check, which the small icon.sys read in vsReadIn passes. vsNameOk callers: 796, 822, 867. vsReadAll callers: 707, 836; vsWriteAll: 743, 887, 889.

findings.title: Stale comments in vmcsaves: header names vmcsaves.c; vsCopy's static save is ~3.9 KB, not ~2.5 KB
findings.problem: vmcsaves.h:4 says 'see vmcsaves.c', but the file is src/core/vmcsaves.cpp. The comment at vmcsaves.cpp:1123 says vs_save_t is ~2.5 KB, but it is 64 vs_file_t of 60 bytes (name[33]+pad, size, two 8-byte stamps, 4-byte pointer) plus ~56 bytes of header, about 3.9 KB of .bss.
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.h 1-55 and vmcsaves.cpp 70-84, 1121-1144. No src/core/vmcsaves.c in the repo (ps2.yaml:641 lists src/core/vmcsaves.cpp). The size uses 32-bit EE pointers and natural alignment, INFERRED rather than measured.
